expected.finding: **[P2]** `scripts/revise-improvement-policy.py`, `candidate_anchor()`: `merged.update(anchor)` overwrites retained evidence counts with `None` when the current policy’s keyword definition differs from the snapshot. When evaluating an ancestor whose definition matches that snapshot, the count remains lost. This can make ancestor validity undefined and suppress a needed rollback. Resolve counts against each candidate’s definitions before applying current-policy unknowns.

**[P2]** `scripts/measure-policy-validity.py`, `measure()` / `anchor_counts_at()`: An initial round without a parseable timestamp retains `timestamp_ms=None`, which `anchor_counts_at()` interprets as “include every trace.” Its historical epoch therefore includes future evidence, contradicting the replay’s temporal boundary. Treat an unknown epoch timestamp as unavailable historical evidence; reserve the unrestricted cutoff for the current measurement.
